speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing issues with your gait and limb coordination; can you tell me when these symptoms first began and if they have been worsening gradually or suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned the clumsiness is especially noticeable on the right side; can you tell me if you have experienced any headaches, nausea, or vomiting alongside these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Natalizumab use carries a significant risk for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), which could explain your neurological symptoms. Have you experienced any cognitive changes, such as memory loss, confusion, or difficulty speaking, in addition to the motor issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of natalizumab use and the asymmetric neurological deficits, I need to rule out PML immediately. REQUEST TEST: Brain MRI with contrast
